items.title: ZenMux Launches DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for High-Throughput Reasoning
items.summary_1line: ZenMux Launches DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for High-Throughput Reasoning USA Today
items.editor_note: ZenMux launches DeepSeek V4.1-Flash for high-throughput reasoning, the first third-party host to pick it up.

editorial.tldr: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash on Sep 10, claiming it beats flagship V4-Pro while cutting the memory agents need to run it. The efficiency claim rattled Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares within a day, and DeepSeek quantified it Sep 13 as a 75% HBM and 87.5% SSD cut.
editorial.whats_new: Third-party host ZenMux added DeepSeek V4.1-Flash for high-throughput reasoning on Sep 22, the first sign the model is spreading to inference platforms beyond DeepSeek's own API.
editorial.why_it_matters: Anyone calling the V4-Pro endpoint is now served different weights than they pinned, at a price that keeps falling, without a version bump to signal either change -- and now a third-party host serves the same model, so routing choices need re-checking too.
editorial.take_for_builders: Re-run your eval suite against the V4-Pro endpoint: you're getting V4.1-Flash's outputs at a still-falling price, and any prompt or behavior tuned to V4-Pro specifically may have silently drifted. If you route through ZenMux or another third-party host, verify it serves the same weights before trusting cross-provider evals.

status.state: Shipped · V4-Pro traffic silently rerouted, now on third-party hosts too
status.detail: V4.1-Flash launched Sep 10 beating V4-Pro on quality while cutting agent memory needs; the efficiency claim rattled memory-chip stocks by Sep 11, and by Sep 14 DeepSeek was routing all V4-Pro traffic to V4.1-Flash at a price that kept falling. A Sep 20 follow-up added the 1M-context/KV-compression specifics behind the architecture, and by Sep 22 third-party host ZenMux was serving the model too.

open_questions: Does the claimed memory-footprint cut hold up in independent agent-workload benchmarks, not just DeepSeek's own numbers?
Will DeepSeek formally deprecate the V4-Pro endpoint, or keep serving V4.1-Flash under the old name indefinitely?
Do outputs from the V4-Pro endpoint show measurable quality or behavior differences now that V4.1-Flash serves them?
Has the 1M-token context and KV-cache compression figure been independently benchmarked, or does it restate DeepSeek's own claims?
Does ZenMux serve the identical weights and config as DeepSeek's own endpoint, or a re-quantized variant with different behavior?
